source: Original (authored 2026-10-28, calculator; early-finisher extension of 2-6Q_Trigonometry, scored separately). Kite ABCD: AB = AD = 10 cm, CB = CD = 7 cm, angle BAD = 1.4 rad.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Kite ABCD, AB = AD = 10, CB = CD = 7, angle BAD = 1.4 rad. Find BD.
parts.tolerance: Accept 12.9 or the display with an ellipsis (12.8843...). Degree mode (0.244) earns A0. A value cut short without an ellipsis earns A0.
parts.notes: M1 for the cosine rule in triangle ABD. A1 for the correct substitution 10^2 + 10^2 - 2(10)(10) cos 1.4. A1 for 12.9.

parts.label: b
parts.tolerance: Accept 2.34 or the display with an ellipsis. Accept any value consistent with the candidate's own correctly-rounded BD, including 2.34 from BD = 12.9. The answer must be in radians: 134 degrees earns A0. A value cut short without an ellipsis earns A0.
parts.notes: M1 for the cosine rule for an angle in triangle BCD. A1 for BD as the side opposite angle BCD: cos C = (7^2 + 7^2 - BD^2)/(2(7)(7)). A1 for 2.34. Wrong method: a sign error gives 0.804: M1A0A0.
parts.follow_through: FT from the candidate's BD in (a).

parts.label: c
parts.description: Find the area of the kite.
parts.tolerance: Accept 66.9 or the display with an ellipsis. Accept any value consistent with the candidate's own correctly-rounded intermediates, e.g. 66.8 from BD = 12.9. A value cut short without an ellipsis earns A0.
parts.notes: M1 for a correct area expression for either triangle (two sides and the angle between them). M1 for adding the two triangles. A1 for 66.9. Other correct methods earn full marks: 2 x (1/2)(10)(7) sin ABC, or half the product of the diagonals. Wrong method: triangle ABD alone (49.3): M1M0A0.
parts.follow_through: FT from the candidate's angle in (b).

parts.label: d
parts.tolerance: Accept 1.27 or the display with an ellipsis. Accept any value consistent with the candidate's own correctly-rounded angle BCD. The answer must be in radians: 72.9 degrees earns A0. A value cut short without an ellipsis earns A0.
parts.notes: M1 for the angle sum 2 pi with angle ABC = angle ADC by symmetry, (2 pi - 1.4 - BCD)/2, or any other valid method (e.g. angle ABD + angle DBC). A1 for 1.27. Wrong method: angle ABD = (pi - 1.4)/2 = 0.871 alone: M0A0.
parts.follow_through: FT from the candidate's angle in (b).

source: Original (authored 2026-10-28, calculator; early-finisher extension, unit 1 statistics). Sunshine x: 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10; drinks y: 12, 19, 14, k, 27, 26; mean of y is 20.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Six (x, y) pairs with y = 12, 19, 14, k, 27, 26; the mean of y is 20. Find k.
parts.notes: M1 for (12 + 19 + 14 + k + 27 + 26)/6 = 20, or the total 120. A1 for 22. Wrong method: dividing by 5 gives k = 2: M0A0.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Find Pearson's r and write down the regression line of y on x, y = ax + b.
parts.tolerance: Accept r = 0.896, a = 1.90, b = 8.57, or the displays with an ellipsis; accept a = 40/21, b = 60/7. A value cut short without an ellipsis earns A0 for that value.
parts.notes: A1 for r = 0.896. A1 for a = 1.90. A1 for b = 8.57. The line must be given as an equation; a and b given without the equation earn A1A0 for the line.
parts.follow_through: FT from the candidate's k in (a).

parts.label: c
parts.description: 24 drinks sold on another day; use the appropriate regression line to estimate the hours of sunshine.
parts.tolerance: Accept 7.68 or the display with an ellipsis, including 7.68 from the rounded coefficients. A value cut short without an ellipsis earns A0.
parts.notes: M1 for choosing the regression line of x on y to estimate x from y. A1 for x = 0.421y - 2.42 (0.421052..., -2.42105...). A1 for 7.68. Wrong method: solving the y-on-x line for x gives 8.10: M0A0A0.
parts.follow_through: FT from the candidate's k in (a).

parts.label: d
parts.description: Write down the coordinates of the intersection of the y-on-x and x-on-y regression lines.
parts.notes: A1 for x = 6 (the mean of x), A1 for y = 20 (the mean of y), independently. 'Write down': no working needed.
